title: BalancerPoolerV2.setPool strands previous pool's BPT
description: V2 made `_pool` mutable (new in V2). `withdrawBPT` calls `IERC20(_pool).transfer(...)`, always against the CURRENT pool address. If owner calls `setPool(newPool)` while the contract still holds BPT of the previous pool, `withdrawBPT` cannot reach the previous pool's BPT — it targets the new pool's BPT token. No generic-token rescue exists. Owner workaround is to round-trip `setPool` back to the old pool, withdraw, then setPool forward again — fragile and error-prone.
impact: Owner assets (previous-pool BPT) become temporarily unreachable through the standard withdrawal path. Since the user explicitly requested that owner be able to withdraw BPT to migrate to V2, this is a direct concern.
attack_path: Owner operational footgun that strands their own assets: setPool is called while previous-pool BPT is still held, and the standard withdrawal path no longer references the correct token.
recommendation: Add a generic `rescueERC20(address token, address to, uint256 amount) onlyOwner`, or change `withdrawBPT` to accept the BPT token address as a parameter rather than reading `_pool`.
